Keywords: anchoring, first clue, fixation, tunnel vision, first error
Description: Fixing on the first plausible cause and filtering later evidence through it.
How It Shows Up: Hours spent on the first suspect; evidence against it explained away.
Countermeasure: Write at least three hypotheses before testing any; record evidence against your favorite.

Keywords: confirmation bias, prove theory, cherry pick, assumptions
Description: Running checks that can only confirm your theory, never refute it.
How It Shows Up: Tests designed to pass; 'it must be X' without a check that could show it is not X.
Countermeasure: For each hypothesis ask what result would prove it wrong, and run that check.

Keywords: streetlight, easy place, convenient, looking where easy
Description: Searching where it is easy to look instead of where the problem is.
How It Shows Up: Reading familiar code and logs while the unfamiliar dependency goes unchecked.
Countermeasure: Let evidence (traces, bisect, profiles) choose where to look next, not familiarity.

Keywords: works locally, environment, my machine, local vs ci, production only
How It Shows Up: Closing bugs that only reproduce elsewhere; dismissing CI failures.
Countermeasure: Reproduce in the failing environment or diff environments systematically.

Keywords: premature optimization, micro optimization, fast enough, performance guess
Description: Optimizing before knowing it matters or where the time goes.
How It Shows Up: Complex caching or clever code with no benchmark.
Countermeasure: Measure first; optimize the biggest measured cost; keep the simple version if numbers do not justify the change.

Keywords: golden hammer, favorite tool, familiar technology, everything is a nail
Description: Using a familiar tool or pattern whether or not it fits.
How It Shows Up: Every problem solved with the same framework, database or pattern.
Countermeasure: List at least two alternatives and why they do not fit before choosing.

Keywords: not invented here, reinvent, build vs buy, write our own
Description: Rebuilding what a well-maintained library already does.
How It Shows Up: Custom date parsing, crypto, retries or HTTP clients.
Countermeasure: Search for a maintained library first; build only with a clear reason.

Keywords: rewrite, second system, start over, from scratch, greenfield
Description: Believing a rewrite will be faster and cleaner than incremental change.
How It Shows Up: Proposals to start over that underestimate edge cases hidden in old code.
Countermeasure: Prefer strangler fig and incremental refactoring; list the behaviors the old code handles first.

Keywords: sunk cost, already invested, keep going, too far to stop
Description: Continuing a failing approach because of time already spent.
How It Shows Up: Days of patching a design that keeps fighting back.
Countermeasure: Time-box approaches; at each box ask whether you would choose this path again starting today.

Keywords: estimate, estimation, deadline, underestimate, how long
Description: Underestimating the time and risk of your own tasks.
How It Shows Up: Estimates that ignore testing, review, migration and unknowns.
Countermeasure: Estimate from similar past tasks; add explicit time for tests, review and rollout; spike unknowns.

Keywords: gold plating, scope creep, extra features, polish, nice to have
Description: Adding features or polish nobody asked for.
How It Shows Up: PRs growing beyond the acceptance criteria.
Countermeasure: Check every addition against the Step 1 criteria; move extras to follow-ups.

Keywords: bikeshedding, trivial, nitpick, style debate, naming debate
Description: Spending attention on trivial, easy-to-judge issues while missing hard ones.
How It Shows Up: Reviews full of naming and formatting comments but no correctness findings.
Countermeasure: Review correctness and security first; leave style to linters and formatters.

Keywords: coverage, coverage percentage, metric, goodhart, test count, assertions
Description: Treating the coverage number as the goal, so tests run code without checking what it does.
How It Shows Up: Tests with no or weak assertions; snapshots of everything; coverage goes up while bugs keep shipping.
Countermeasure: Name the behavior each test guards and the bug it would catch; break the code once to see the test fail; use mutation testing on critical code.

Keywords: understanding, explain, assumption, names, documentation, mental model
Description: Believing you understand code from its names, comments or docs without tracing what it actually does.
How It Shows Up: Explanations that paraphrase function names; surprise when a simple-looking function has side effects.
Countermeasure: Trace a real input through the code, run it or a test, and back every claim with file:line.
